comment: She's super intelligent and passionate about her field, but during lectures she'd just go off on a 20 minute tangent about who-knows-what and it often got really tiring. When she wasn't rambling, her discussions and input were really interesting and valuable and her grading was a tad tough, nothing crazy.

I took one of Dr. Simpon's courses on prisons. The topic is worth discussing but not with her. She loses focus in discussions and simply goes on tangents (including about her personal life) that prevent critical analysis of the texts in class. Yet she is still hard and picky grader, with super high standards for papers. Do not recommend.

The Wire FYS is one of the best they offer, few readings and a really cool topic that can lead to interesting tangents. However, they grade ruthlessly hard for a really informal class. I love my FYS but it makes no sense that it's a class I have the lowest grade in. Unless you give them exactly what they want your grade is gonna be hurt.

I took The Wire. She presents her opinion as fact, and multiple times told me "No, you're so wrong" when I disagreed with her (again, on matters of opinion). I feel like it's pretty childish for a professor to use a class simply as a means to boost her ego. Show up, be quiet, and do the work and you'll pass. The show is great though!

Had her for WGSS 200 too and plan to take her again. She really cares about students, and always brings a unique perspective to class (she goes off on a lot of tangents, but they're always interesting). While very opinionated, she's open to other stances as long as you can back up your argument -- she will call you out if you can't (as she should).

Professor Simpson assigns grades arbitrarily. She laughs and her turns her head up at students when their views do not conform to her own. The class has no structure. She can be fun but should more receptive to students and opinions. She is very rude in her style of teaching.

I would not recommend taking her. She is very opinionated. In class it felt like she wasn't taking her job seriously. It feels like she was just going through the motions. She did very little to teach material. If you pay to come to this school, you should receive better teachers. Her exams are ok. Half on textbook the other half is what she says.

Loved this class. Dr. Simpson was a very opinionated and entertaining professor. Studying government is usually a rather boring endeavor but that was not the case with this course. Don't go into her exams with the expectation of just having to regurgitate what you read. Be prepared to apply it to real world examples and current events. TAKE. NOTES.
Took the wire with her. Great teacher. Fair amount of work. Opinionated, but every academic is, so nothing unusual.
Really great professor. Good for progressive-minded students. Don't take if you don't have an open mind. Interesting debates throughout. Participation is required if you want to get a good grade.

Lectures do get offf topic but she really keeps you entertained. Grading is difficult to understand and you need to keep reminding her to give papers back to you. Overall great professor for progressive minded students.  You'll learn a lot.

Lectures go totally off-the-wall and often go into utter irrelevancy. But if you participate, understand basic concepts of politics and listen to midtermexam review, it's easy. Unavoidable as she is only Intro to American Gov't professor, class is tolerable at best.

Dr. Simpson is an incredible professor, and you will be hard-pressed to meet a more charismatic and hilarious woman. She is incredibly passionate about racial and social justice issues so I would recommend her to any progressive-minded individuals. I have never learned so much from a professor and have recommended her to every one of my peers.

Worst teacher I have ever had. She is extremely biased and will focus only on the plight of african americans. I wrote the majority of my assignments with a conservative slant to test if she would grade fairly. I had an F most of the semester. I caught her taking more points off my tests for the same answers my classmates had.

Hands down best teacher I had at Richmond. She is opinionated, but helps you learn how to formulate arguments. Her expectations are crystal clear - if you meet/slightly exceed them you will get an A. She was a theatre major in college so she's very engaging. She's also very, very smart. STRONGLY recommended.
Very liberal. Picks favorites. Often only tells one side of an issue, and sometimes looks/talks down to those that do not agree with her. Good sense of humor though.
learned a lot...maybe a few too many personal stories but they set the stage...sincerely wanted us to learn and interpret for ourselves

Imparts her own political views and beliefs into your grades.  Fails to be objective in class (or for grades) and spins lectures with her own viewpoint- brushes aside student's comments that are different from her politcal beliefs. Talks of her own personal experiences than of scholarly work-- annoying boastful.

She's an amazing teacher. I learned a lot and thoroughly enjoyed her class. If you pay attention to her lessons and the news, you will do well. She's a really cool lady too. I'd say it was my favorite class since I've been at Richmond. -PS

Professor Simpson is very nice and helpful.  Her class can be tough but you'll be fine as long as you read the books and keep up with current events.  She really wants all her students to do well, and is very willing to help students who might be having trouble.

She is heavily biased-ONLY TAKE HER if you are extremely liberal-she'll hate you if you aren't.  She can't teach a class without trying to push her views onto everyone else.  She picks favorites and her grading system is ludacris.  She also repeats herself a lot and retells stories that she forgets she already told.  Worst prof I've had at UR

Comes off like she is a hard-ass but ended up a relatively gentle essay grader. tests are not too bad. occasionally witty, more often talking about herself or important people she supposedly knows. first test is hard then once you know what too expect the course is pretty easy
I didn't sign up for Race Politics, I signed up for American Government. Simpson is very opinionated, and if your opinion doesn't coincide with hers, then you're screwed.

Simpson makes class entertaining with her humor. If you know your stuff, you can do A-work. However, if you have no interest in doing the reading/keeping up on current events, she is not your professor. Otherwise, she's more engaging than any other American Gov option.

Do NOT take this professor. She is an extremely unfair grader and is very close minded. She teaches things in the class that have absolutely nothing to do with American Government. There is only one right answer with her and she gives no room for your own interpretation. Stay away from her at all cost. I hvent met anyone who enjoyed her class.

Didn't really focus on American Govt. as much as race and the civil rights era. VERY opinionated, first exam was pretty tough, had to make a new one to make up for bad grades. Final was pretty straight forward. VerY CRItical on papers but ended up giving most people good grades. Don't take if you have another option.
Amazing teacher, extremely interesting, class is challenging though
unfair grades, unclear assignments, thinks the world is oppressing her

Be prepared for attack if you're conservative.I'm not so I found her rants entertaining.Lessons,texts race-based.Grew up during Civil Rights Movement.Underlying message:"minorities are oppressed" but was hidden behind "be critical of government".Difficult exams.Tough,very fair grader.Completely shot down on 1st paper grade.Liked her class a lot.

She goes beyond the the boring basics of learning terms and memorization. She forces students to analyze topics and think critically. Her style of teaching educates students more than any other way of teaching. Its a hard course but good grades are achievable with help from prof Simpson.Recomended!
Very contradictory in writing assignments.  Also, does not really teach American Government.  More of a political media class.  Very opinionated, unfair paper grader.
